title: Reconstructing the stellar mass distributions of galaxies using S4G IRAC 3.6 and 4.5 micron images: II. The conversion from light to mass
extraction: Online HTML available; full paper not retained in tracked packet.
supported_claims: BC03/Chabrier old-star models support a color-independent 3.6-micron M/L of 0.6 with approximately0.1dex accuracy; the full model grid gives0.11dex, and the narrower0.06dex estimate assumes an age-metallicity relation. Eq4 is log10Υ=3.98(±0.98)c+0.13(±0.08), where c is Vega [3.6]-[4.5]. The calibration assumes old stellar light with nonstellar contamination removed. Vega zero points are280.9/179.7Jy and solar magnitudes3.24/3.27.
checks: Source/version authenticated; formula and restrictions extracted; application conditional.
verdict: Conditional: supports population-calibration sensitivity envelopes on clean light; does not measure this object's radial M/L or justify independent per-annulus calibration errors.

title: The Spitzer Survey of Stellar Structure in Galaxies: Precise Stellar Mass Distributions from Automated Dust Correction at 3.6 micron
extraction: Online HTML available; full paper not retained in tracked packet.
supported_claims: The adopted mass conversion is0.6 for dust-corrected old-star3.6-micron luminosity with Chabrier IMF and approximately0.1dex accuracy. Eq7 instead estimates an effective galaxy-integrated M/L against original integrated color: log10(M/L)=-0.339(±0.057)c-0.336(±0.002), calibrated for -0.1<c<0.15. The authors recommend approximately0.2dex uncertainty for that empirical relation. It is not automatically a spatially resolved intrinsic M/L law.
checks: Source/version authenticated; distinctions between clean-light and empirical original-light conversions extracted.
verdict: Conditional: a clean-light conversion is applicable with explicit population/IMF assumptions; the original-color regression is not used as an object-specific radial prior.

title: A unified picture of breaks and truncations in spiral galaxies from SDSS and S4G imaging
extraction: Online HTML tables available; NGC5023 plotted profile inspected. No numerical full color profile recovered.
supported_claims: NGC5023 has measured projected SDSS optical and3.6-micron profiles. At the103.7arcsec break, Table4 lists g-r=0.36AB and r-band surface brightness22.56ABmag/arcsec²; typical break-color error is0.10mag. The adopted distance is9Mpc and slit width1.2kpc. The optical mass conversion is log10Υr=-0.306+1.097(g-r)-0.15. Authors caution that dust and line-of-sight mixing complicate intrinsic interpretation.
checks: Source/version authenticated; object table values, band, aperture and calibration extracted.
verdict: Verified independent projected color evidence; intrinsic radial3.6-micron M/L bounds remain unverified without extinction/deprojection and band conversion.

title: The Optical and Near-Infrared Properties of Galaxies: I. Luminosity and Stellar Mass Functions
supported_claims: The optical color relation uses diet-Salpeter normalization. Subtracting0.15dex corresponds approximately to Kroupa/Kennicutt normalization. The absolute diet-Salpeter scale was constrained using maximum-disk considerations, so it is not a purely photometric absolute calibration.
verdict: Adjacent calibration only; not used here to impose an independent absolute radial mass bound.

title: Extragalactic archeology with the GHOSTS Survey I. Age-resolved disk structure of nearby low-mass galaxies
supported_claims: HST F606W/F814W age-selected star counts resolve NGC5023's radial structure. Table4 gives inner radial scale lengths/vertical sech² scale parameters in kpc: MS8.46/0.21, upperHeB23.42/0.20, lowerHeB19.15/0.20, AGB1.66/0.31, RGB1.84/0.42;3.6-micron1.24/0.30. The age-selection calibration uses synthetic CMDs with constant SFH and flat metallicity distribution; counts-to-flux conversion is described as approximate because the real SFH is unknown. These are population structural fits, not a calibrated radial M/L profile or normalization. Quoted table entries lack individual fit errors.
checks: Source/version authenticated; radial versus vertical quantities distinguished.
verdict: Verified independent resolved population geometry; no justified numerical annular M/L bounds extracted.

title: Analysis of spatially resolved stellar populations and emission line properties in nearby galaxies with J-PLUS data. II. Results for the M51 group and first comparison with the M101 group
extraction: Online HTML available; plotted population/error maps exist; numerical maps not obtained.
supported_claims: The twelve-band J-PLUS DR3 analysis includes NGC5023 with log10M*=8.75 and Mr=-17.55AB at8.59Mpc. It uses AlStar with updatedBC03 populations, Chabrier IMF, and two-component Calzetti attenuation (birth-cloud optical depth1.27times ISM). Fluxes are perturbed in100 MonteCarlo runs; an effective r-band S/N ceiling50 is imposed. Maps are projected and no coherent population-color pattern is asserted for the low-mass galaxies. Numerical intrinsic radial M/L/error bounds were not recovered.
checks: Version/metadata authenticated; IMF, dust, distance and uncertainty method extracted. Public numerical-map acquisition incomplete.
verdict: Verified independent resolved population study and global mass estimate; annular intrinsic M/L application remains unverified.

title: IRSA S4G pipeline products for NGC5023
authors: S4G collaboration; P5 summary M.Querejeta and S.Meidt
identifier: P5 September2014 release; IRSA dataset doi:10.26131/IRSA425
supported_claims: Six numerical ellipse-profile tables and stellar/color/ICA-mask FITS images exist and were downloaded. P5 is an old-stellar-emission map, not a direct mass map. Cleaned color is constant where ICA correction is applied. The summary has acceptable qualityflag2, stellar fraction0.742115 and stellar source color-0.137080±0.013892 within its stated analysis area. P3 brightness-specific columns include aperture corrections and AB-magnitude errors.
checks: Official archive documentation and object files retrieved; file hashes verified; FITS header OBJECT=ngc5023, image type old-stellar3.6-micron source confirmed.
verdict: Verified independent spatial photometry; radial intrinsic M/L measurement not implied by the product.

title: SIMBAD NGC5023 identification record
supported_claims: Record explicitly lists both NGC5023 and UGC8286; ICRS position13h12m11.8036s,+44d02m17.3287s. Local SPARC and S4G table coordinates agree at catalog-center precision.
verdict: Verified alias. The inconsistent PGC alias printed in the2026 article is not used.
